reasoning:
I'm weighing the proposed changes: introducing a fixed target_colour field, updating target_cube by anchoring to the carried value near target_colour rather than reopen-point matching, adding a ledger for swap tracking, and keeping target_cube as a subgoal even when it's missing from the resting list. I want to cross-check these against what happened in earlier rounds, starting with why round 1 was refused.

Looking more closely, round 1's refusal was about refreshing from the released cube since the carried value only drifted due to shuffle derivation — but since the cube is always returned to its original spot, anchoring to carried value should give equivalent results in correct episodes while avoiding drift. Round 3's reopen-point matching, which was added to handle a brief occlusion, actually failed later when fingers reopened mid-air near other cubes, so carried-value anchoring resolves that case too without reintroducing the mid-air drift problem. So this change settles round 3 cleanly, though it does partially roll back round 1's refresh-from-released-cube logic — I need to think through whether that reversal is actually safe given round 1's original reasoning.

The ledger's starting position should match the put-down spot, which checks out, and I should add the subgoal line too. Now I'm drafting the exact wording for the annotator prompt edit — specifying that at later decision steps, a put-down is detected by the gripper descending and reopening, with the released cube identified as the nearest listed cube at that frame rather than relying on mid-air coordinates, falling back to proximity-based matching otherwise.

For the policy prompt, there are two edits to make: replacing the swap prose section with the ledger logic, and updating the later-step passage to clarify that the robot returns the cube to its original spot, using the nearest resting cube of the target colour within tolerance, and never relying on gripper or held/lifted coordinates to locate it.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: Always point at target_cube as updated at this step.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: Always point at target_cube as updated at this step. When target_cube is absent from the resting list at this step (held or still settling), still point at target_cube itself, never at any other listed cube.

policy_prompt_for_memory.description: At the first decision step (memory empty) write the colour word of the cube identified as the picked cube in the demonstration (the listed cube nearest the gripper at the lowest frame where the fingers first read about 46%): 'red', 'blue', 'green', or 'cube' when the list has no colours. At every later step copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. blue

edits.modify_from: Then carry the 'picked' label through the shuffle one swap at a time. A swap is a run of frames in which exactly two listed positions leave their resting spots and, when the list is still again, the same two spots are filled again: the two movers have EXCHANGED spots. If the picked cube was one of the two movers, it is now on the OTHER mover's starting spot, never back on its own. If it was not a mover, it stays put. Do not use mid-crossing frames to decide where it lands; they only tell you a swap is happening. Repeat for every swap to the last demonstration frame, however many swaps occur and whatever partners they involve: two consecutive swaps of the same pair return it to its original spot; a swap of a different pair moves it elsewhere or leaves it alone, so it can end two or more spots from where it started. Do not decide by which cube is 'back' on the original pick spot: once any swap has touched that spot, the cube resting there afterwards is a different cube. Write the position of the labelled spot as listed in the scene at the start of execution.
edits.modify_to: Then track the picked cube through the shuffle as a written ledger; do not read it off the final list. Step 1: write the pick spot P (the listed cube nearest the gripper at that lowest frame) and the spot where the cube is put back down (the listed cube reappearing beside the gripper when the fingers reopen); call that spot L. Step 2: go through the remaining demonstration frames. A swap is a run of frames in which exactly two listed spots are vacated and, when the list is still again, the same two spots are filled again: the two movers have EXCHANGED spots. Each time this happens write one ledger line 'swap: spot X <-> spot Y; L now = ...': if L equals X write Y, if L equals Y write X, otherwise L is unchanged. Mid-crossing frames only tell you a swap is happening; never use them to decide where L lands. Continue to the last demonstration frame however many swaps occur and whatever partners they involve (two consecutive swaps of the same pair return L to its original spot; a swap of a different pair moves it again or leaves it alone, so it can end two or more spots from where it started). Step 3: after the last frame, write the listed position in the scene at the start of execution nearest L (within about 10 px). Never write the cube resting on P when P appeared in any swap line: once any swap touched that spot, the cube resting there is a different cube.

edits.modify_from: At every later decision step: if the execution steps shown include a frame where the gripper is at about height 0.02 with fingers partly closed and the fingers then reopen to about 100% at that height (a put-down), the released cube is the listed cube in the scene at this decision step that lies nearest the gripper's own [y, x] at that reopen frame: write that listed position. If it is absent from the list for a frame or two while the gripper rises over it, that is occlusion, not a sign that another listed cube is it; never locate it from 'held in the gripper' or 'lifted off the table' coordinates, which drift in mid-air. Otherwise write the position of the listed cube within about 10 px of the carried value, or copy the carried value if none is listed. Ignore 'lifted off the table' lines.
edits.modify_to: At every later decision step: the robot always puts the cube back where it picked it, so write the position of the resting listed cube of target_colour within about 8 px of the carried value. If there is none (the target is held in the gripper, occluded under the gripper, or listed only as 'lifted off the table' while it settles), copy the carried value unchanged. Do not locate it from the gripper position at the reopen frame, nor from 'held in the gripper' or 'lifted off the table' coordinates, which drift in mid-air. Never relocate to a cube of another colour or to a different resting cube nearby.

Otherwise the value is the position of the listed cube nearest the previous value (within about 10 px), or the previous value unchanged if none is listed. 'Lifted off the table' lines are ignored.

The gripper's position at the reopen frame, 'held in the gripper' coordinates and 'lifted off the table' coordinates are never used to locate it, and the value never moves to a resting cube of another colour or to a different resting cube nearby.
